k160: Gemrift Privacy Policy — how Gemrift handles local save data, Microsoft Store licensing, and your privacy.
k164: Effective Date: March 2026 • Publisher: Bulent Ozkir • App ID: 9P3QHCNQ5SL3
k165: Gemrift ("we", "our", or "us") is a Windows puzzle-action cave adventure developed and published by Bulent Ozkir. We respect your privacy and designed both this website and the Gemrift desktop game so you can play without surrendering personal data.
k167: No Personal Data Collection: Neither the Gemrift game nor this website collects, sells, rents, or transmits personally identifiable information (such as your name, email address, phone number, contacts, or precise location).
k168: No Accounts or Tracking SDKs: Gemrift does not require user registration, login credentials, third-party analytics trackers, or advertising cookies.
k169: 2. Local Game Data on Your Device
k170: Gemrift stores your game settings, unlocked caves, difficulty selections, and high scores locally on your Windows PC under your user profile (%APPDATA%\Gemrift\save.json). When you watch built-in cave solution recordings ("Show me resolution"), the game streams the MP4 walkthrough over HTTPS and caches it locally in %LOCALAPPDATA%\Gemrift\ RecordingsCache so subsequent views play offline. You can delete these local files at any time by uninstalling the app or clearing the folders.
k172: Gemrift is distributed via the Microsoft Store (https://apps.microsoft.com/detail/9p3qhcnq5sl3?hl=en-US&gl=US) with a 1-day free trial and a paid full version unlocking the complete 215-cave campaign and all solution videos. Billing, trial status verification, and license management are handled directly by Microsoft through the Windows Store APIs. Microsoft's own Privacy Statement governs transactions and Store telemetry.
k174: This website is hosted statically on GitHub Pages. We do not set tracking cookies or run analytics scripts. Standard web server logs (such as IP addresses requested for security and content delivery) are processed by GitHub in accordance with the GitHub Privacy Statement.
k176: Gemrift is a family-friendly cave puzzle adventure featuring Milo Coppercap. Because the game and website do not collect personal data from any user, we do not knowingly collect personal information from children under the age of 13.
k178: If you have any questions about this Privacy Policy, please reach out via the Gemrift GitHub repository.

ux.miniMapBody: A small aerial photo of the whole cave sits in the top-right corner of the cave view. The mini map shows the real cave as seen from above, with its dirt, rocks, gems, creatures and water, and it changes as the cave does. The white box marks the part of the cave you can see, and the bright dot with a ring is Milo. When Milo walks behind the map, it turns see-through. It is shown in every cave until you close it: press Ctrl+X, or click the X button on its corner. Press Ctrl+Z to show it again. It stays shown or hidden the way you left it, in the next caves too.
ux.solutionsTitle: Need a little light? Solution recordings
ux.solutionsBody: Levels 1-5 recordings are free for everyone. From level 6 onward, the bulb stays visible; an active full-game Microsoft Store license and two failed attempts on the same cave unlock recordings for every cave, including ones already cleared. After 9 failed attempts on one cave, that cave's recording also unlocks for everyone, on Windows and Mac, with or without the full game. Failures are saved per cave across sessions and difficulties; manual restarts, quitting, and skipped caves do not count, though a gate retry can count as another failed attempt. Click the bulb to watch only that cave's downloaded, verified MP4. It loops automatically; Replay starts it again, and Close returns to the paused game. On a Mac the recording opens in your video player instead, and the game waits until you click Close. Missing recordings and failed license checks are reported.
